## Construct an internal angle bisector {#fv2-construct-angle .fv-lesson .proof-lesson .construction-slide }

```{=html}
<div data-vector-construction="angle" data-initial-text="Use equal lengths along the two sides.">
<p class="construction-given"><strong>Recall:</strong> A diagonal of a rhombus bisects its opposite angles.</p>
<p class="construction-given">Let <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}=\overrightarrow{AB},\quad \underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{AC}"></span>.</p>
<div class="construction-layout">
<div class="construction-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Triangle ABC with side vectors a and b."></div>
<ol class="construction-steps" aria-label="Construction working">
<li hidden data-step-text="Make a unit vector along AB."><span class="construction-step-label">1. Make a unit vector along AB.</span><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{u}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}}{|\underset{\sim}{a}|},\qquad |\underset{\sim}{u}|=1"></span></li>
<li hidden data-step-text="Make a unit vector along AC."><span class="construction-step-label">2. Make a unit vector along AC.</span><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{v}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|},\qquad |\underset{\sim}{v}|=1"></span></li>
<li hidden data-step-text="Translate and add the two unit vectors."><span class="construction-step-label">3. Translate and add the two unit vectors.</span><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{v}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}}{|\underset{\sim}{a}|}+\frac{\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|}"></span><span class="construction-step-note">The equal-length sides form a rhombus.</span></li>
<li hidden data-step-text="Scale the diagonal to meet BC at D."><span class="construction-step-label">4. Scale the diagonal to meet BC at D.</span><span data-math="\overrightarrow{AD}=k(\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{v}),\quad k>0"></span><span class="construction-step-note">Choose <span data-math="k"></span> so that <span data-math="D"></span> lies on <span data-math="BC"></span>.</span></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="construction-controls"></div>
</div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Supports booklet p. 14 · unit vectors</div>

::: {.notes}
Begin by recalling that a diagonal of a rhombus bisects its opposite angles. This does not hold for a general parallelogram. Step 1 draws u=a/|a|, and step 2 draws v=b/|b|. Both have unit length; the diagram represents them at the same common scale. Step 3 translates v to the head of u, and u to the head of v, forming a rhombus. Its diagonal u+v therefore bisects the angle at A. Step 4 scales that direction until it reaches BC at D: AD=k(u+v), where k>0 is chosen for this intersection. No calculation of k or dot-product verification is needed. The sum u+v gives the direction; its tip need not be on BC. Do not assume a+b bisects the angle when |a|≠|b|.
:::
